title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over number fields
main_claim: Let G be an absolutely almost simple, simply connected group over a number field k. Then every noncentral abstract normal subgroup N of G(k) equals δ_A^{-1}(W), where W is some open normal subgroup of the product of G(k_v) over the finitely many nonarchimedean places v at which G is anisotropic. The paper proves the cases the literature had left open: anisotropic outer type A, trialitarian D4 and E6. It also states a corollary, the congruence subgroup property in Rapinchuk's positive-density setting.

issues.location: sections/colors.tex, 'Local abelianization and the metaplectic input', Eq. (colors-metaplectic)
issues.description: The circle-extension step depends on an injectivity statement: H^2_m(prod_{v in A} S(k_v), R/Z) -> H^2(S(k), R/Z) is injective. The paper says this is the 'V_2 = empty' specialization of Prasad–Rapinchuk, Prop. 2.6. The local groups SL_1(D_v) have nontrivial continuous characters (the T_v of Lemma colors-local-abelianization), so H^2 of the finite product has Kunneth cross terms. Injectivity on those cross terms therefore rests entirely on the cited proposition applying to a finite product of anisotropic local factors with S(k) embedded diagonally. I could not check that against the source. The application itself looks consistent.
issues.evidence: "This is the specialization V_2=\varnothing of \cite[Proposition~2.6, p.~114]{PRmetaplectic}."

issues.location: sections/exceptional-types.tex, Lemma d4-local-openings and Lemma e6-root-involution
issues.description: Rational noncentral or root involutions are obtained from Borovoi Prop. 3.4(i), with only archimedean local points checked. This uses the version of the Hasse principle that, for a simply connected G and a connected semisimple stabilizer, needs no finite-place hypothesis. That is believable (the p-adic H^2 classes are neutral), but it is quoted, not proved. The real-place checks themselves are correct: compact rank at least 3 for D4, and the minus-type F_2 quadratic form argument for E6.
issues.evidence: "Borovoi's theorem ... requires only archimedean local points to conclude X(k)\ne\varnothing \cite[Proposition~3.4(i)]{Borovoi}."

issues.description: Which class (8A or 8B) has cycle shape 1^2.2.8 depends on which of the two degree-12 representations is used, since the outer automorphism swaps them. The argument only needs some order-8 element of that shape with centralizer of order 8, and such an element exists, so this is a labeling issue only.

coverage:
I read all eight LaTeX sections in full (about 5,700 lines) and checked them step by step.

Computational checks with numpy/sympy:
- The noncommutative difference-function identities (the Sylvester solution, the z-move identities, A'*A'=q+q*, and the three-unitaries product m_b m_z m_e*).
- The formula for z' in the boost lemma.
- The identity U(s)L(t)U(-s/u)L(-tu)=diag(u,1/u).
- In the palette section: z unitary and commuting with w, [vw,uz]=1, [w^{-1}v,z^{-1}u']=1, the z formula, the translation formula b_w(s), and the Cayley conjugate of diag(xi,1/xi).
- The PSU_3 count identity in the finite-group lemma, and the symplectic regular-unipotent matrix.
- The even-degree quaternion identities: ss'+s's=2r(2h-1), jb=-bj, b^2=4j^2h(1-h), and equal characteristic polynomials of the diagonal blocks of h.

Checked by hand:
- The finite-defect reduction, the affine sieve and power-factor approximation (codimension and single-pole Frobenius splitting), cyclic detection, the sign-extension lemma, and the S_m x C_2 norm torus.
- Commuting approximation (codimension bound, Newton polygon, Jordan derangement argument), class preservation, Feit–Seitz, and the circle-extension construction (local abelianization, discrepancy coboundary, residue commutator surjectivity with the gcd computation, Eisenstein norms).
- The no-characters argument (well-definedness, transitivity, pure shears, additive span lattice argument, signature normalization, path/mesh argument).
- The palette measure (conformal weights, harmonic-function Jensen argument, base measure equal to m, Howe–Moore step, approximation of V_0), the recurrence lemma (spectral atom bound, van der Corput, Weyl), the thickness/Szemeredi argument, and generation of left rotations by squares (multiplier formula and linear independence).
- The finite-group families: point-pair test, A_n cycle choices, PSL_l, PSL_2, the abelian-test counting, the sporadic table (spot-checked), the unitary count lemma, symplectic/orthogonal/PSU blocks, the exceptional tori with primitive-prime and Hadamard index bounds, E_7, Suzuki/Ree and 2F4.
- Unitary induction (ternary Chatelet argument, odd matrix generation, Hermitian quadratic subfield via Borovoi, the factorization u=wq, local norm and pole tests, degree-four multinorm correction), the D4 involution-product argument and cyclic H^2 vanishing, and the E6 generic D4 dimension count, pullback and torsor.

Not checked: the original statements of the cited external theorems (Prasad–Rapinchuk Prop 2.6, Borovoi, Langlands convergence, Fulman–Guralnick, ATLAS data beyond spot checks).
sibling_notes: The board for family 018 had one entry, the companion global-function-field paper (rank 18), reported as no_gap_found. It checked the same shared machinery: arithmetic reduction, power-factor approximation, the norm-torus lattice including m=4, the circle extension, the palette identities and the finite-group appendix with its sporadic table. That agreed with my independent checks of the parallel number-field arguments, and I did not rely on it for any step. I posted my own verdict to the board.
